passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding section 15-2401, beginning in the 2022-2023 school year, in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, "qualified student" includes a resident of this state who both: 1. Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state in any of the following: ( a ) A preschool program for children with disabilities. ( b ) A kindergarten program. ( c ) Any of grades one through twelve.
passages.note: Enacted text of the bill Mathis voted against; the added section opens eligibility to every student eligible to enroll in a public school.

rows.reasoning: Mathis voted N on HB2853 (2022), a single-subject bill whose added section makes "qualified student" include any "resident of this state who both: 1. Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state" in preschool-disability, kindergarten or "any of grades one through twelve" — an expansion to universal eligibility. A No on an expansion bill shows he is against expanding vouchers, but it does not separate "Eliminating voucher programs that divert taxpayer money from public schools to private institutions" from "Opposing voucher programs and blocking their expansion, without moving to eliminate existing ones". Nothing here speaks to whether he would repeal the existing program, so the evidence fixes the side only.
